subject: Urgent: service surge impact, remediation plan & settlement conversation
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@firmax.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Cc: ops@firmax.com
Date: 2028-05-31T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike: production latency & errors impacting inference pipeline

Connor / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained degradation across our inference traffic starting late Friday night (UTC). Key impacts:
- 95th/99th tail latency jumped from ~220ms -> 3.2s for our primary routing; impacts web response times and downstream batch workers.
- Error rate (5xx) spiked to ~6% for two 45-minute windows; retries caused backpressure and queueing.
- Effective throughput dropped ~38% during peak windows, causing backlog and failed scheduled workflows.

We need an immediate remediation plan and we want senior exec visibility. This caused missed SLAs with our customers and put revenue at risk for the weekend sales campaigns. Please confirm:
1) Root-cause analysis ETA and temporary mitigation you can apply in the next 2 hours.
2) A commercial remedy — credits for the impacted period and a timeline for any contract amendment.
3) Exec call availability (we prefer 09:30 PT today) — we want CRO/Head of Ops level.

I've attached a short CSV with request traces and our preliminary impact numbers.

Lena
Lena Ortiz
VP, Platform Engineering — Firmax Inc.

Immediate steps (what we'll do now):
- Incident triage: I'm looping in Ben (CS/ops lead) for remediation and short-term routing changes.
- Exec coordination: Marissa (account lead) will join the call to discuss commercial relief.
- I'll organize an exec bridge at 09:30 PT and invite our Head of Infrastructure. If that time doesn't work for you, propose an alternative.

I'll follow up within 30 minutes with an initial mitigation plan.

–Connor
Connor O'Brien

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, lena.ortiz@firmax.com
Cc: support@redwood.com, infra-oncall@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-31T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: production latency & errors impacting inference pipeline

Lena / team — Ben here. We're seeing correlated symptoms in our metrics. Quick summary from infra:
- Internal ticket INF-9871 opened.
- Timeline: 22:12 UTC Fri -> first latency uptick; two major windows 22:40–23:25 UTC and 02:10–02:55 UTC.
- Root-cause hypothesis: a regression in autoscaler scheduling combined with a rare model-variant cache eviction pattern; under high-concurrency load the scheduler mis-allocated some GPU capacity causing tail amplification.

Immediate mitigations applied: 
1) Manual routing to warm model variant (lower request concurrency per instance) — mitigated tail latency for 80% of traffic within 12 minutes.
2) Disabled the aggressive autoscaler policy that appears correlated with the scheduling behavior.
3) KVs reclaimed & cache primed for the affected model version.

Next steps for remediation (ETA in hours):
- Deep RCA (logs + kernel metrics): 24–48 hours.
- Permanent configuration change + safe canary for autoscaler: 72 hours.
- We will generate a transcript of every impacted request and correlate with your traces.

Commercial/credits note: we'll produce a quantified impact report for the affected windows and present a credit calculation for the incident. That will be on the exec call.

–Ben Carter
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

1) Contract reference: Section 5.2 (SLA & credits) defines the credit formula as a percentage of monthly fees prorated by the SLO breach window; we'll need to run the exact arithmetic against Firmax's May invoice and the impacted token/embedding units.

I'll have finance on standby for the arithmetic and can share a rough calculation within 24 hours.

- We're asking for an interim credit to be applied to our June invoice while you finalize the formal calculation. A provisional 8% credit for May's bill would be acceptable to our CFO as an interim measure.

Lena Ortiz
